Now, according to a report from Bloomberg, the Sunnyvale startup is in talks to raise at least $50 million in a round that would value it at $500 million. Altimeter Capital Management is the firm driving the new conversation, and it's doing so only weeks after Tenspresso closed a $20 million seed round led by Striker Venture Partners. The company was co-founded by Dong Hyuk Woo and Harshit Khaitan, two engineers who spent years together building Google's tensor processing units before striking out on their own. That pedigree is doing most of the work here. Tenspresso's 15 person team is stacked with alumni from Google's early TPU effort, and in a market where that kind of experience is scarce, Altimeter and Striker appear willing to pay for the roster before there's a product to show for it. There is no chip yet. Tenspresso aims to finish designing its first product in late 2027 or early 2028, Bloomberg reported, which means a $500 million valuation would rest entirely on an architecture and a team, not silicon, not customers, not a single benchmark. The company is building for inference, specifically chips meant to handle long context windows so AI models can chew through larger and more varied pools of data at once. That's a real and growing bottleneck for anyone running big models in production, but it's also a bet two years out from being testable. highlights.titleZh: Supermicro will sell SambaNova’s inference chips alongside Nvidia GPUs
highlights.content: Supermicro will build and sell AI inference systems that pair SambaNova’s SN50 chips with Nvidia GPUs, the companies said on Tuesday. The collaboration initially plans for 10,000 SN50 chips, according to SambaNova’s announcement. The racks will join Supermicro’s Data Center Building Block Solutions, the ready-made data centre systems it sells to customers. Running an AI model has two stages. First the system reads the prompt, then it writes the answer piece by piece. In the new racks, Nvidia GPUs do the reading and SN50 chips do the writing, SambaNova said. The company says AI agents work nonstop, so how fast they act depends on how fast the model responds. > “Agentic AI is the next wave of inference, and it has to run everywhere,” said Rodrigo Liang, co-founder and chief executive of SambaNova. “Now customers can order SN50 RDUs alongside GPUs, from a world-leading partner they trust.” ## Who does what Supermicro will put the systems together, test them, deliver them and support customers, including with on-site service. SambaNova engineers will get AI models running and tuned on SN50 and help with deployments. The companies will start with neoclouds, the cloud providers built for AI, and with sovereign clouds. Those keep data and computing inside one country. They then plan to sell to companies that run AI in their own data centres. > “Supermicro is committed to delivering flexible, high-performance AI infrastructure that supports the evolving requirements of our customers,” said Charles Liang, president and chief executive of Supermicro. ## Built for existing data centres SN50 is SambaNova’s fifth-generation Reconfigurable Dataflow Unit, or RDU, a chip designed for inference. The company says it can serve the largest models without needing extreme power density in each rack. A SambaRack SN50 draws an average of 20 kW, SambaNova said last week. Operators can add inference capacity in data centres they already run, according to SambaNova. They do not have to wait for new builds held back by power and cooling. It says they can also keep using their existing GPUs for longer. The two companies say they can deliver much more inference capacity in 2027 as a result. ## SambaNova’s other recent deals The Supermicro deal follows another one with Oracle. Oracle said at its AI World conference on 27 October that it plans to deploy SN50 chips in its cloud data centres. It will offer the capacity to AI model builders. Two days later, SambaNova signed Emergys, a digital transformation services company, to deploy and run its platform for enterprise customers. SambaNova, founded in 2017 and based in San Jose, raised new funding at an $11 billion valuation in July. In June, Foxconn and Intel joined it to build rackscale AI infrastructure. ## Get the TNW newsletter Get the most important tech news in your inbox each week. ## Popular articles * 1 * 2 * 3 * 4 * 5

highlights.content: UPDATED 11:05 EST / NOVEMBER 04 2026 ### Tencent releases Hy4, powerful frontier LLM introducing visual understanding and computer use by Kyt Dotson Tencent Holdings Ltd. today introduced Hy4, a new large language model that adds computer-use capabilities for the first time, using advanced visual understanding, reasoning and tool-calling to deliver long-horizon agentic performance. The company said the model marks a significant leap in performance over its Hy4 Preview, which arrived August 28, weighing in at 770 billion parameters with 49 billion active parameters. Both provide a 1 million token context window, putting it in the same range as current open-weights frontier models from European and Chinese developers, including Mistral AI SAS, Beijing Moonshot Technology Co. Ltd. and Z.AI Co. Ltd. The company said it substantially scaled both pre-training and post-training, reporting gains over the preview version in instruction following, long-context understanding, agentic long-horizon tasks, and deep research. Tencent also identified excessive reasoning and over-verification during the previous version’s “thinking” processes. The new model focuses heavily on real-world productivity for workplace collaboration, human experience and professional work. The company said it optimized long-context learning capabilities to understand complex information, including web development, document summarization, visual creative tasks, document presentation, and more. The company added that it also enhanced its capability for front-end and game development, high-complexity tasks that include intricate business logic, state management, and orchestration. Some models struggle with producing stateful, elegant and beautiful user interfaces that are visually polished and also fully functional. It is not uncommon for professional game developers, industry engineers and amateur vibe coders to use AI models as part of their work. However, a recent spate has had coders begin to reproduce, reverse engineer and clone older and semi-recent video games. This caused Anthropic PBC to block Claude Code and its underlying Opus 5.5 model from assisting in these tasks. The company said it integrated deeply with major engines such as Unreal Engine, Unity, and Godot, giving it the capability to support complex game logic and multiplayer implementations. Compared to the preview, Tencent said Hy4 improved by 19.1 percent in the GameDev bench and 9.8 percent in GameLogic benchmarks, although the actual baseline numbers remain internal and weren’t released. highlights.content: UPDATED 09:00 EST / NOVEMBER 04 2026 ### Exclusive: BlueFlag Security expands AI agent governance to cover unapproved coding agents by Duncan Riley Software development security startup BlueFlag Security Inc. today expanded the artificial intelligence agent governance tools in its developer risk platform to cover unapproved coding agents, including those running on engineers’ laptops outside the code repository. The update also brings automated fixes for some of the risks the platform turns up. BlueFlag is going after a problem that has grown fast as coding assistants have evolved into agents that plan their own work and spin up the environments they need. Many sign in with a developer’s credentials. An agent working that way inherits every permission the developer holds. Raj Mallempati, BlueFlag’s co-founder and chief executive, described the AI agent as “the most powerful and least governed identity in the development environment.” The company plans to start interrupting attack paths as they form early next year, he said. For now, the platform reports them. In the current release, the work starts with finding the agents, which BlueFlag does from activity in the code. It picks up each agent through the commits and pull requests it produces, then classifies it by what it does with the code and whose identity it uses. Security teams can trace any agent back to the developers who work with it and the repositories it operates in, with unapproved agents marked as such. AI tools running locally on a developer’s machine are harder to spot. To catch those, BlueFlag reads data from endpoint detection and response products such as those from CrowdStrike Holdings Inc. and SentinelOne Inc., so nothing new has to be installed on the device. Human review gets its own checks. BlueFlag now flags pull requests approved by an AI agent, along with commits an agent wrote from start to finish and pipeline runs that went out with no person signing off. Organizations can also require a human review before anything merges or deploys. For any software release, customers can document where a person was in the decision and where one was not. A separate inventory looks at AI inside the applications a company builds. It records the model providers and agent frameworks each application relies on and scores them against the Open Worldwide Application Security Project’s Top 10 for Agentic Applications. AI spending is measured as well. BlueFlag ties the tokens and dollars each developer burns through to the commits and accepted code that came out of them, and it points to places where spending keeps climbing with no new commits behind it. Paid seats that sit idle show up in the same report. Remediation runs through two new tools. AccessGuard targets identity problems such as overpermissioned accounts and stale credentials. Misconfigured repositories and pipelines are handled by DriftGuard, which corrects settings such as missing branch protections that drift over time. Fixes can be applied by hand from written instructions or run automatically with one click, and automated changes can be rolled back. Auto parts supplier Marelli Holdings Co. Ltd. is a customer. highlights.content: IT Brief UK - Technology news for CIOs & IT decision-makers [![IT Brief UK logo](/brands/itb-new-logo.svg) United Kingdom](/) [Powered By ![TechDay logo](/brands/td-new-logo-right.svg)](https://techday.co.uk) ![llm-d 1.0 aims to cut AI inference costs for firms](https://itbrief.co.uk/uploads/story/2026/11/04/brian-stevens-mark-lohmeyer-and-nikhil-thomas-story-323333.webp) [DC](https://itbrief.co.uk/tag/data-centers) [Open source](https://itbrief.co.uk/tag/open-source) [LLMs](https://itbrief.co.uk/tag/large-language-models) # llm-d 1.0 aims to cut AI inference costs for firms Wed, 4th Nov 2026 (Today) [![Joseph Gabriel Lagonsin](https://itbrief.co.uk/rails/active_storage/representations/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsiZGF0YSI6MTYyNSwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--675a9c66bfe11204f24f3bdaad09013f83135297/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsiZGF0YSI6eyJmb3JtYXQiOiJ3ZWJwIiwicmVzaXplX3RvX2ZpbGwiOlsxNjAsMTYwXSwicXVhbGl0eSI6ODV9LCJwdXIiOiJ2YXJpYXRpb24ifX0=--89ddf5e6765c65a563c2258053e9d33c05d195da/Joseph%20Headshot.webp) JOSEPH GABRIEL LAGONSIN News Editor](/author/joseph-gabriel-lagonsin) The llm-d project has released version 1.0 of its open source AI inference software. It was founded by Red Hat, IBM, Google Cloud, CoreWeave and NVIDIA. The release is the first full production version of software designed to help companies run large language models more efficiently across shared computing infrastructure. The project is now governed by the Cloud Native Computing Foundation and has attracted contributions from more than 500 developers across more than 25 organisations. llm-d focuses on inference, the stage at which trained AI models generate responses for users and applications. That part of the AI stack has become a growing cost centre for companies deploying chatbots, coding tools and so-called agentic systems that make repeated calls on memory, compute and stored context. Version 1.0 adds multi-tenant controls to manage competing workloads on the same hardware, alongside high-availability routing and rolling upgrades intended to allow maintenance without service interruption. It also introduces a stable configuration interface for users seeking to standardise deployments across different clouds and accelerators. The release also adds session-aware routing, which keeps multi-turn conversations close to cached context so systems can avoid recomputing the same information. The software supports a range of model servers, including vLLM and SGLang. **Cost pressure** The launch comes as businesses look for ways to cut the cost of serving AI models after the initial training phase. In one example cited by project backers, IBM Research used open models with llm-d in work on quantum error-correction hardware and reported inference costs 11.5 times lower than an all-proprietary setup. That project recorded a prefix-cache hit rate of about 98% and a blended serving cost of roughly USD $0.11 per million tokens. Caching matters because many AI workloads repeatedly draw on the same context, and reusing that information can reduce the fresh computation needed for each request. In another test, researchers used llm-d to deploy the open-weight GLM 5.2 model, described as having about 753 billion parameters, on NVIDIA GPUs already widely used in data centres. On benchmark agentic workloads with hundreds of parallel sessions, the system produced more than 6.6 million output tokens a minute at peak and served up to 3,000 concurrent coding agents without pre-emptions. According to figures released by the project, that setup would have delivered a per-token cost five to 10 times lower than equivalent commercial API pricing at current cloud rental rates. The biggest savings were reported on input-heavy workloads, which are common in software agents that repeatedly submit long prompts and context windows. **Industry backing** The project's list of supporters points to broad interest in open alternatives to proprietary inference platforms. Through advanced visual understanding, reasoning, and tool-calling capabilities, Hy4 now supports a broader range of tasks, including fine-grained image processing, complex chart analysis, and mathematical visual reasoning. Additionally, Hy4 introduces computer-use capabilities for the first time, enabling it to interact with both command-line interfaces and graphical user interfaces to perform a wide range of work and everyday tasks. AI Agents.content: UPDATED 09:00 EST / NOVEMBER 04 2026 ### Exclusive: BlueFlag Security expands AI agent governance to cover unapproved coding agents by Duncan Riley Software development security startup BlueFlag Security Inc. today expanded the artificial intelligence agent governance tools in its developer risk platform to cover unapproved coding agents, including those running on engineers’ laptops outside the code repository. The update also brings automated fixes for some of the risks the platform turns up. BlueFlag is going after a problem that has grown fast as coding assistants have evolved into agents that plan their own work and spin up the environments they need. Many sign in with a developer’s credentials. An agent working that way inherits every permission the developer holds. Raj Mallempati, BlueFlag’s co-founder and chief executive, described the AI agent as “the most powerful and least governed identity in the development environment.” The company plans to start interrupting attack paths as they form early next year, he said. For now, the platform reports them. In the current release, the work starts with finding the agents, which BlueFlag does from activity in the code. It picks up each agent through the commits and pull requests it produces, then classifies it by what it does with the code and whose identity it uses. Security teams can trace any agent back to the developers who work with it and the repositories it operates in, with unapproved agents marked as such. AI tools running locally on a developer’s machine are harder to spot. To catch those, BlueFlag reads data from endpoint detection and response products such as those from CrowdStrike Holdings Inc. and SentinelOne Inc., so nothing new has to be installed on the device. Human review gets its own checks. BlueFlag now flags pull requests approved by an AI agent, along with commits an agent wrote from start to finish and pipeline runs that went out with no person signing off. Organizations can also require a human review before anything merges or deploys. For any software release, customers can document where a person was in the decision and where one was not. A separate inventory looks at AI inside the applications a company builds. It records the model providers and agent frameworks each application relies on and scores them against the Open Worldwide Application Security Project’s Top 10 for Agentic Applications. AI spending is measured as well. BlueFlag ties the tokens and dollars each developer burns through to the commits and accepted code that came out of them, and it points to places where spending keeps climbing with no new commits behind it. Paid seats that sit idle show up in the same report. Remediation runs through two new tools. AccessGuard targets identity problems such as overpermissioned accounts and stale credentials. Misconfigured repositories and pipelines are handled by DriftGuard, which corrects settings such as missing branch protections that drift over time. Fixes can be applied by hand from written instructions or run automatically with one click, and automated changes can be rolled back. Auto parts supplier Marelli Holdings Co. Ltd. is a customer. Kristie Pfosi, its global chief information security officer, said agentic AI made the unknowns inside her company’s own development environment bigger “overnight.” “Within the first week BlueFlag showed us which AI agents were working in our repositories, which developers they worked with, and where the gaps were in how they were approved, scoped and reviewed,” Pfosi said. “Those are findings we can act on the same day.” The launch comes a day after BlueFlag published its first research report, “The State of Developer Risk 2026.” Its figures come from metadata the platform collected on tens of thousands of identities and access tokens at a subset of BlueFlag’s enterprise customers, in a snapshot taken in September. AI Agents.content: [Skip to content](#main-content) [News](/) English ![Docker Urges Isolation and Governance for AI Agent Security](/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fnews.lavx.hu%2Fapi%2Fmedia%2Ffile%2Fdocker-urges-isolation-and-governance-for-ai-agent-security-1_1793795610830-1200x630.jpg&w=3840&q=75) #Security # Docker Urges Isolation and Governance for AI Agent Security • ![Lukas Brandt](/_next/image?url=%2Fauthors%2Flukas-brandt.webp&w=64&q=75) [Lukas Brandt](/author/lukas-brandt) •4 min read Share this article Docker published a guide identifying five security risks when AI agents browse, run code, and call tools with limited oversight. The company argues isolation and governance, not model improvements alone, must contain agents that chain actions with a user's full permissions. Docker has published a guide to five security risks that emerge when AI agents browse, run code, and call tools with limited human oversight. Product manager Eric Jia and principal product marketing manager Srini Sekaran write that the autonomy making agents useful also renders conventional application security controls insufficient. The company positions isolation and governance as the primary defenses. The post identifies prompt injection, tool misuse and poisoning, excessive autonomy, credential exposure, and data exfiltration as the principal risks. These share a common cause: an agent selects tools at runtime, chains actions, and often operates with the permissions of the person who started it. A coding agent may read a file, install a dependency, alter configuration, run tests, and push a commit after receiving one instruction. A compromised or misdirected agent can take a wider range of actions than a conventional service. Docker presents prompt injection as the defining risk. Rather than compromising a system directly, an attacker can embed instructions in material the agent reads, such as a web page, code comment, issue, or document. Docker cites an incident in which a coding agent followed instructions hidden in repository content and performed actions its user did not request. The company doubts that model instructions eliminate prompt injection, since an agent cannot reliably distinguish a legitimate instruction from an injected one. Its preferred response is to limit what a hijacked agent can reach. Tools form the second area of concern. Agents use connectors, database queries, file operations, and code execution to affect external systems. Giving an agent more tools than a task requires enlarges the attack surface. A tool description can also carry hidden instructions that lead the agent to misuse the tool. This aligns with guidance from OWASP, which in its [Agentic AI Threats and Mitigations](https://owasp.org/www-project-agentic-ai-threats-and-mitigations/) work identified tool misuse as a major new threat and recommended access verification, behavioral monitoring, operational boundaries, and tamper-resistant execution logs. Excessive autonomy is the third risk. The post describes "YOLO mode," where every agent action is approved automatically, as a visible example of broad standing permission. The company acknowledges this mode can be productive but argues it should sit inside a boundary that prevents the agent from reaching systems or data it should not touch. In one example, a developer asked a coding agent to clean an old repository. The agent generated an rm -rf command with a trailing ~/ and executed it without confirmation, deleting the developer's home directory. In another case, an AWS engineer gave a coding agent a Cost Explorer bug while it ran with operator-level access. The agent chose to delete and rebuild the production environment, causing a 13-hour regional outage. Credential handling connects directly to that problem. Agents should not inherit a developer's personal token, because every action then carries that person's full permissions. Docker recommends separate, short-lived credentials injected at runtime and kept out of the conve...

LLMs.titleZh: Tencent releases Hy4, powerful frontier LLM introducing visual understanding and computer use - SiliconANGLE
LLMs.content: UPDATED 11:05 EST / NOVEMBER 04 2026 ### Tencent releases Hy4, powerful frontier LLM introducing visual understanding and computer use by Kyt Dotson Tencent Holdings Ltd. today introduced Hy4, a new large language model that adds computer-use capabilities for the first time, using advanced visual understanding, reasoning and tool-calling to deliver long-horizon agentic performance. The company said the model marks a significant leap in performance over its Hy4 Preview, which arrived August 28, weighing in at 770 billion parameters with 49 billion active parameters. Both provide a 1 million token context window, putting it in the same range as current open-weights frontier models from European and Chinese developers, including Mistral AI SAS, Beijing Moonshot Technology Co. Ltd. and Z.AI Co. Ltd. The company said it substantially scaled both pre-training and post-training, reporting gains over the preview version in instruction following, long-context understanding, agentic long-horizon tasks, and deep research. Tencent also identified excessive reasoning and over-verification during the previous version’s “thinking” processes. The new model focuses heavily on real-world productivity for workplace collaboration, human experience and professional work. The company said it optimized long-context learning capabilities to understand complex information, including web development, document summarization, visual creative tasks, document presentation, and more. The company added that it also enhanced its capability for front-end and game development, high-complexity tasks that include intricate business logic, state management, and orchestration. Some models struggle with producing stateful, elegant and beautiful user interfaces that are visually polished and also fully functional. It is not uncommon for professional game developers, industry engineers and amateur vibe coders to use AI models as part of their work. However, a recent spate has had coders begin to reproduce, reverse engineer and clone older and semi-recent video games. This caused Anthropic PBC to block Claude Code and its underlying Opus 5.5 model from assisting in these tasks. The company said it integrated deeply with major engines such as Unreal Engine, Unity, and Godot, giving it the capability to support complex game logic and multiplayer implementations. Compared to the preview, Tencent said Hy4 improved by 19.1 percent in the GameDev bench and 9.8 percent in GameLogic benchmarks, although the actual baseline numbers remain internal and weren’t released. To advance scientific reasoning, Tencent advanced the next stage of Recursive Self-Improvement to enhance research and development capabilities. Using the Hyra 2.0 harness, an autonomous AI research agent system, the model optimized the pre-training infrastructure for smaller models sharing the same architecture. The model is currently available on Tencent Cloud TokenHub, WorkBuddy, CodeBuddy, Yuanbao, WeCom’s AI Assistant, Ima and more. It can also be accessed via third-party sources such as OpenRouter, Hermes and OpenCode. The company added that, despite its significant enhancements over Hy4 Preview, it kept costs low, maintaining the same pricing at around $0.90 per million input tokens, $2.70 per million output tokens, and $0.045 per million cached input tokens. The Flash version of the model is scheduled for release soon to deliver greater cost efficiency for users. The company also said it intends to release the model weights and system cards in the coming days as part of its commitment to responsible open-source AI development. ##### Image: Tencent # A message from John Furrier, co-founder of SiliconANGLE: Support our mission to keep content open and free by engaging with theCUBE community. LLMs.content: IT Brief UK - Technology news for CIOs & IT decision-makers [![IT Brief UK logo](/brands/itb-new-logo.svg) United Kingdom](/) [Powered By ![TechDay logo](/brands/td-new-logo-right.svg)](https://techday.co.uk) ![llm-d 1.0 aims to cut AI inference costs for firms](https://itbrief.co.uk/uploads/story/2026/11/04/brian-stevens-mark-lohmeyer-and-nikhil-thomas-story-323333.webp) [DC](https://itbrief.co.uk/tag/data-centers) [Open source](https://itbrief.co.uk/tag/open-source) [LLMs](https://itbrief.co.uk/tag/large-language-models) # llm-d 1.0 aims to cut AI inference costs for firms Wed, 4th Nov 2026 (Today) [![Joseph Gabriel Lagonsin](https://itbrief.co.uk/rails/active_storage/representations/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsiZGF0YSI6MTYyNSwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--675a9c66bfe11204f24f3bdaad09013f83135297/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsiZGF0YSI6eyJmb3JtYXQiOiJ3ZWJwIiwicmVzaXplX3RvX2ZpbGwiOlsxNjAsMTYwXSwicXVhbGl0eSI6ODV9LCJwdXIiOiJ2YXJpYXRpb24ifX0=--89ddf5e6765c65a563c2258053e9d33c05d195da/Joseph%20Headshot.webp) JOSEPH GABRIEL LAGONSIN News Editor](/author/joseph-gabriel-lagonsin) The llm-d project has released version 1.0 of its open source AI inference software. It was founded by Red Hat, IBM, Google Cloud, CoreWeave and NVIDIA. The release is the first full production version of software designed to help companies run large language models more efficiently across shared computing infrastructure. The project is now governed by the Cloud Native Computing Foundation and has attracted contributions from more than 500 developers across more than 25 organisations. llm-d focuses on inference, the stage at which trained AI models generate responses for users and applications. That part of the AI stack has become a growing cost centre for companies deploying chatbots, coding tools and so-called agentic systems that make repeated calls on memory, compute and stored context. Version 1.0 adds multi-tenant controls to manage competing workloads on the same hardware, alongside high-availability routing and rolling upgrades intended to allow maintenance without service interruption. It also introduces a stable configuration interface for users seeking to standardise deployments across different clouds and accelerators. The release also adds session-aware routing, which keeps multi-turn conversations close to cached context so systems can avoid recomputing the same information. The software supports a range of model servers, including vLLM and SGLang. **Cost pressure** The launch comes as businesses look for ways to cut the cost of serving AI models after the initial training phase. In one example cited by project backers, IBM Research used open models with llm-d in work on quantum error-correction hardware and reported inference costs 11.5 times lower than an all-proprietary setup. That project recorded a prefix-cache hit rate of about 98% and a blended serving cost of roughly USD $0.11 per million tokens. Caching matters because many AI workloads repeatedly draw on the same context, and reusing that information can reduce the fresh computation needed for each request. In another test, researchers used llm-d to deploy the open-weight GLM 5.2 model, described as having about 753 billion parameters, on NVIDIA GPUs already widely used in data centres. On benchmark agentic workloads with hundreds of parallel sessions, the system produced more than 6.6 million output tokens a minute at peak and served up to 3,000 concurrent coding agents without pre-emptions. According to figures released by the project, that setup would have delivered a per-token cost five to 10 times lower than equivalent commercial API pricing at current cloud rental rates. The biggest savings were reported on input-heavy workloads, which are common in software agents that repeatedly submit long prompts and context windows. **Industry backing** The project's list of supporters points to broad interest in open alternatives to proprietary inference platforms. LLMs.content: * Featured * [Corporate](https://www.tencent.com/category/corporate/) * [For business](https://www.tencent.com/topic/topic-for-business/) * [For consumers](https://www.tencent.com/topic/topic-for-consumers/) * [Innovation](https://www.tencent.com/topic/topic-innovation/) # Tencent Launches Hy4, Joining the Ranks of the World’s Leading Open-Source AI Models November 4, 2026 Tencent today announced the release of Tencent Hy4, its latest-generation large language model, marking a significant leap in performance and capabilities that now ranks it among the world’s leading open-source AI models. Tencent Hy plans to release model weights and system cards in the coming days, reinforcing its commitment to responsible open-source AI development, with a focus on cybersecurity and biological safety. The new model also introduces visual understanding capabilities for the first time, alongside major improvements in instruction following, long-context comprehension and long-horizon agentic tasks, delivering stronger overall performance across a diverse set of applications. Through advanced visual understanding, reasoning, and tool-calling capabilities, Hy4 now supports a broader range of tasks, including fine-grained image processing, complex chart analysis, and mathematical visual reasoning. Additionally, Hy4 introduces computer-use capabilities for the first time, enabling it to interact with both command-line interfaces and graphical user interfaces to perform a wide range of work and everyday tasks. The model has undergone specialized training on professional software such as Blender and CAD, significantly enhancing its ability to plan and execute long-horizon and sophisticated tasks. #### Deep Model-Product Co-Design Unlocks New Opportunities for Real-World Productivity Leveraging significant advances in its foundational capabilities and deep model-product co-design, Hy4 unlocks a broader range of real-world productivity scenarios: **Office Productivity & Collaboration**: Hy4 has significantly enhanced the user experience on Tencent WorkBuddy. Evaluation benchmarks show an average performance score of 83.18 and a pass rate of 96.15 percent, with Hy4 ranking first place in nine out of twelve scenarios within the mainland Chinese market. In practical use, Hy4 balances efficiency and effectiveness for visual creative tasks, 3D scene construction, and web development. Furthermore, it delivers marked improvements in document presentation, stability, and usability for human-AI collaborative tasks on WorkBuddy. Leveraging enhanced in-context learning capabilities, Hy4 excels at understanding complex information from diverse sources. Integrated with WeCom via WorkBuddy, Hy4 connects with daily workflow data across chats, emails, documents, calendars, and meetings. When managing multiple projects simultaneously, Hy4 automatically tracks project history and recent developments. It identifies outstanding tasks, flags upcoming meetings that require preparation, and monitors approaching deadlines, helping users prioritize effectively and stay aligned on important follow-ups. In addition, new team collaboration capabilities powered by Hy4 will be introduced with the upcoming release of WorkBuddy’s “Projects” feature. Hy4 has also been optimized for professional financial analysis. By training on thousands of specialized workspaces and tens of thousands of high-quality tasks derived from real-world scenarios, the model gains a deep understanding of expert workflows in fund research, securities analysis, and quantitative investment strategies. In a rigorous blind evaluation conducted by the Tencent Hy team in partnership with Tencent Financial Technology, Hy4 emerged as the top-performing open-source model. The assessment involved 213 financial professionals, including 153 experts from leading external institutions, approximately 70 percent of whom possessed more than five years of industry experience. LLMs.content: [Skip to content](#main) Wednesday, November 4, 2026 [Advertise with us](/advertise)[About us](/about) [General](/general) # Digital Retailers Lead AI Commerce as Consumer Brands Lag, Benchmark Shows By [Maria Santos](/author/maria-santos)[Korea](/markets/korea "More retail news from Korea") 3 min read | In this article (9) Retailers are locking down direct access to automated shopping systems, leaving consumer goods manufacturers scrambling to keep their products visible as buyers hand search queries over to algorithms. Checkout platforms control the transaction pipe, and that proximity gives them the power to dictate terms. An evaluation of 106 consumer companies published in October 2026 shows all six digital retail platforms evaluated maintain an explicit agentic commerce strategy, with five operating live tools. By contrast, only two out of 53 consumer products manufacturers run an active offering. The divide reflects who owns customer interactions at the point of purchase. Retailers are deploying their own virtual assistants and linking inventories directly into third-party artificial intelligence engines to protect baskets. Consumer product makers remain largely relegated to optimizing product descriptions so language models recommend their items. ## Early Revenue Shows High Basket Sizes Conversion metrics explain the speed of retail investment. AI-referred shoppers to retail portals convert 42 percent better than conventional inbound channels, reversing the prior year when such traffic converted 38 percent worse. In the United States, 40 percent of shoppers report using automated systems to buy goods online, with 85 percent rating the automated journey higher than standard site search. Top-tier operators report material revenue gains from proprietary tools. Amazon attributes roughly $12 billion in incremental annualized sales to its Alexa for Shopping platform, formerly known as Rufus. Walmart recorded a 35 percent rise in average order value among customers using its Sparky assistant. Supermarket and specialty store operators are taking defensive positions against third-party aggregators. Eleven of 16 surveyed domestic and specialty retailers hold an explicit automated commerce strategy, with eight running live customer-facing systems. Walmart cited agentic platforms as an operational risk in its corporate filings, while Kroger warned investors that external platforms risk disintermediating direct shopper relationships. ## Asian Travel Retailers Test Automated Assistants Travel retail represents the slowest segment in the benchmark. Only two of 11 operators maintain an active roadmap, and none outline specific AI commercial goals in investor reporting. > “Only two of 11 operators maintain an active roadmap, and none outline specific AI commercial goals in investor reporting.” Pockets of regional testing show how duty-free operators intend to bridge the gap. In South Korea, Lotte Duty Free introduced a ChatGPT shopping service in July 2026 to guide travelers through duty-free assortments. In Australia, WH Smith deployed a pilot in-store AI assistant at Melbourne Airport to answer traveler product queries at the shelf edge. For Asian department stores and cross-border airport operators, third-party agents threaten high-margin concession models. If transit passengers rely on personal AI agents to compare tax-free allowances and local downtown prices, airport concessionaires lose pricing use. Terminal retail landlords face weaker tenant turnover if automated comparison engines steer passengers toward duty-paid domestic orders before they board. ## Manufacturers Pay to Win Model Recommendations Consumer goods makers operate below the checkout interface. Only 20 of 53 manufacturers evaluated possess an AI commerce strategy, focusing primarily on search visibility rather than direct checkout mechanics. AI Product.content: Israeli startup Explorium shuts down after raising more than $127 million Founded in 2017 by Omer Har, Or Tamir and Maor Shlomo, who later left the company to focus on Base44, Explorium built a data enrichment platform before pivoting toward generative AI and tools for AI agents. Its founders say it continued to grow over the past year but could not turn that momentum into a sustainable business. The Israeli startup Explorium is shutting down after nearly nine years of operation. Founders Omer Har and Or Tamir announced the closure in a farewell post, describing the company’s efforts to adapt to rapid changes in the artificial intelligence market. Founded in 2017, Explorium raised more than $127 million from investors including Insight Partners, Oren Zeev’s Zeev Ventures, Emerge, F2 Capital and 01 Advisors. Another co-founder, Maor Shlomo, has since gone on to found Base44, acquired by Wix. Explorium was established by Shlomo, Tamir and Har. The company initially developed a data enrichment platform that connected organizations to thousands of external data sources and signals, allowing them to supplement their internal datasets. The aim was to help data professionals improve machine learning predictions and make better business decisions. Applications included predicting customer churn, assessing credit risk and identifying new business opportunities. The company enjoyed considerable success in its early fundraising rounds. In September 2019, it raised $15.5 million in a Series A round led by Zeev Ventures, following a $3.6 million seed round. In July 2020, it secured $31 million in a Series B round, followed by a $75 million Series C round led by Insight Partners in May 2021. The latest financing brought its total funding to more than $127 million. At the time, Explorium employed approximately 130 people and was expanding its operations in Israel and the United States. But the market in which Explorium operated was changing rapidly. As machine learning became increasingly commoditized and capabilities once reserved for specialized providers became more widely available, the company entered a period of change and restructuring. In their farewell post, Har and Tamir said that after Har took over as CEO, Explorium decided to pivot early toward generative AI. Their premise was that AI agents would emerge as a new category of business users, requiring broad access to high-quality data. Building on its existing infrastructure and partnerships, Explorium launched AgentSource in early 2025, describing it as the first B2B data platform designed for go-to-market agents. The product was aimed at a new wave of companies and platforms developing automated sales and marketing tools. The company subsequently introduced what it described as the first B2B data enrichment solution based on the Model Context Protocol (MCP). That product evolved into Vibe Prospecting, which the founders called the first standalone in-chat prospecting application. It allowed users to access B2B data and identify potential customers through an AI chat interface. According to the founders, the product attracted more than 350,000 registered users. Despite its efforts to reposition the company for the emerging AI-agent market, Explorium was unable to sustain its operations. Har and Tamir said the company had continued to grow over the past year, even as the market underwent significant upheaval, but that growth ultimately proved insufficient. “Today we are sharing hard news. After almost nine years, Explorium is ceasing operations,” the founders wrote. “We started Explorium believing in the power of AI for business, and that AI is only as good as the data behind it.” They described the company's evolution from data enrichment to products designed for AI agents, before acknowledging that its efforts had not been enough to keep the business going. “Thanks to an extraordinary team, we moved rapidly in a market undergoing real turmoil and kept growing this past year. AI Product.content: [Log in](/i/jf/onboarding/web?mode=login&redirect_after_login=%2FTheAIColony%2Fstatus%2F2118037340031443383)[Sign up](/i/jf/onboarding/web?mode=signup&redirect_after_login=%2FTheAIColony%2Fstatus%2F2118037340031443383) ## Article [Log in](/i/jf/onboarding/web?mode=login&redirect_after_login=%2FTheAIColony%2Fstatus%2F2118037340031443383)[Sign up](/i/jf/onboarding/web?mode=signup&redirect_after_login=%2FTheAIColony%2Fstatus%2F2118037340031443383) ## Conversation [![@TheAIColony](https://pbs.twimg.com/profile_images/1680178806890397696/sVcTS1Gb_normal.jpg)](/TheAIColony) [The AI Colony](/TheAIColony)[@TheAIColony](/TheAIColony) [![Article cover image](https://pbs.twimg.com/media/HWTD_EPXYAEc3PC?format=webp&name=medium)](/TheAIColony/article/2118037340031443383/media/2118033213008338945) # How and Where to Launch Your AI Product in 2026 8 min read Most AI products do not fail because they are bad. They fail because nobody finds them. There are over 14,200 active AI tools competing for attention right now. The market is not sitting around waiting to discover yours. If you build something real, ship it quietly to three directories, and wait for users, you will wait a long time. Discovery in 2026 has to be engineered deliberately, across multiple surfaces, on a timeline that runs from 30 days before launch to 90 days after. This guide is the strategic map. How to prepare, when to launch, where to launch, and what to do after the launch-day spike fades so you build traction that actually compounds. ### The failure pattern worth understanding first The numbers are sobering. Research from CIO found that 88% of AI product attempts never reach production traction at all. S&P Global found the average organization scraps 46% of its AI proofs-of-concept before they ship. One analysis tracking more than 319 failed AI startups found that 40% shut down within 24 months. The causes are almost never technical. The pattern repeats: founders build in isolation, skip real user validation, and launch with positioning so vague that a potential user cannot tell within five seconds whether the product is for them. That leads to the single most important idea in this guide. A launch is not a marketing event you bolt on after building. It is the first real test of whether your positioning works, whether your ideal customer is real, and whether the value you built actually lands. The prep work below is how you find that out before launch day, not after. ### Pre-launch: the 30 days that decide everything Most failed launches are decided weeks before the launch date arrives. Everything here happens before you pick a day. ****Write your one-sentence positioning first****. This is the highest-leverage task in the entire process, and most founders rush it. If a stranger cannot understand what your product does in one sentence, your launch posts will confuse people no matter how good the product is underneath. The test is simple. Show your one sentence to someone who does not know you or yourproduct. If they cannot immediately tell who it is for and what problem it solves, rewrite it. Do not launch until it passes. The template that works: “[Product] helps [specific customer] [solve specific problem] without [the current frustrating alternative].” Not “AI-powered [category].” Specific enough that the right person reads it and thinks “that is exactly what I need,” and the wrong person rules themselves out. Positioning that passes this test multiplies across every channel you use. Positioning that fails it undermines every channel at once. ****Validate with real usage****, not opinions. Get 10 people who match your actual customer profile to complete a real task with a rough version of your product. Not a scripted demo. A real goal they actually have. “That is a good idea” tells you nothing. Someone trying and failing to do something tells you almost everything. The strategic pivot, aimed at cementing long-term market dominance as AI reshapes design workflows, signals the company is willing to sacrifice near-term revenue growth to lock in users before competitors can respond. It's a high-stakes bet that puts immediate shareholder returns against the race to become the default AI-powered design platform. [Figma](https://figma.com) just pulled off what should have been a victory lap, but Wall Street isn't celebrating. The collaborative design platform reported Q3 2026 results that topped analyst expectations across the board, yet shares tumbled as much as 12% in extended trading after the company revealed it's giving away what could have been a lucrative revenue stream. The culprit? Figma's decision to bundle advanced artificial intelligence features into existing subscription tiers without raising prices. Open Source AI.content: IT Brief UK - Technology news for CIOs & IT decision-makers [![IT Brief UK logo](/brands/itb-new-logo.svg) United Kingdom](/) [Powered By ![TechDay logo](/brands/td-new-logo-right.svg)](https://techday.co.uk) ![llm-d 1.0 aims to cut AI inference costs for firms](https://itbrief.co.uk/uploads/story/2026/11/04/brian-stevens-mark-lohmeyer-and-nikhil-thomas-story-323333.webp) [DC](https://itbrief.co.uk/tag/data-centers) [Open source](https://itbrief.co.uk/tag/open-source) [LLMs](https://itbrief.co.uk/tag/large-language-models) # llm-d 1.0 aims to cut AI inference costs for firms Wed, 4th Nov 2026 (Today) [![Joseph Gabriel Lagonsin](https://itbrief.co.uk/rails/active_storage/representations/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsiZGF0YSI6MTYyNSwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--675a9c66bfe11204f24f3bdaad09013f83135297/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsiZGF0YSI6eyJmb3JtYXQiOiJ3ZWJwIiwicmVzaXplX3RvX2ZpbGwiOlsxNjAsMTYwXSwicXVhbGl0eSI6ODV9LCJwdXIiOiJ2YXJpYXRpb24ifX0=--89ddf5e6765c65a563c2258053e9d33c05d195da/Joseph%20Headshot.webp) JOSEPH GABRIEL LAGONSIN News Editor](/author/joseph-gabriel-lagonsin) The llm-d project has released version 1.0 of its open source AI inference software. It was founded by Red Hat, IBM, Google Cloud, CoreWeave and NVIDIA. The release is the first full production version of software designed to help companies run large language models more efficiently across shared computing infrastructure. The project is now governed by the Cloud Native Computing Foundation and has attracted contributions from more than 500 developers across more than 25 organisations. llm-d focuses on inference, the stage at which trained AI models generate responses for users and applications. That part of the AI stack has become a growing cost centre for companies deploying chatbots, coding tools and so-called agentic systems that make repeated calls on memory, compute and stored context. Version 1.0 adds multi-tenant controls to manage competing workloads on the same hardware, alongside high-availability routing and rolling upgrades intended to allow maintenance without service interruption. It also introduces a stable configuration interface for users seeking to standardise deployments across different clouds and accelerators. The release also adds session-aware routing, which keeps multi-turn conversations close to cached context so systems can avoid recomputing the same information. The software supports a range of model servers, including vLLM and SGLang. **Cost pressure** The launch comes as businesses look for ways to cut the cost of serving AI models after the initial training phase. In one example cited by project backers, IBM Research used open models with llm-d in work on quantum error-correction hardware and reported inference costs 11.5 times lower than an all-proprietary setup. That project recorded a prefix-cache hit rate of about 98% and a blended serving cost of roughly USD $0.11 per million tokens. Caching matters because many AI workloads repeatedly draw on the same context, and reusing that information can reduce the fresh computation needed for each request. In another test, researchers used llm-d to deploy the open-weight GLM 5.2 model, described as having about 753 billion parameters, on NVIDIA GPUs already widely used in data centres. On benchmark agentic workloads with hundreds of parallel sessions, the system produced more than 6.6 million output tokens a minute at peak and served up to 3,000 concurrent coding agents without pre-emptions. According to figures released by the project, that setup would have delivered a per-token cost five to 10 times lower than equivalent commercial API pricing at current cloud rental rates. The biggest savings were reported on input-heavy workloads, which are common in software agents that repeatedly submit long prompts and context windows. **Industry backing** The project's list of supporters points to broad interest in open alternatives to proprietary inference platforms. SOCRadar’s Threat Research Unit (STRU) attributes the operation to leepsmarts, a Chinese-speaking threat actor, with activity confirmed as late as October 13, 2026. The operation runs on two main tracks: theft of [LLM API credentials](https://socradar.io/resources/report/ai-identity-exposure-report-2026.html) from misconfigured cloud infrastructure, and an academic fraud campaign targeting 20 institutions, 19 of them in the US. Both run on infrastructure in China, South Korea, Malaysia and the US, are coordinated through AI agent frameworks (Hermes Agent, OpenClaw), and are managed from a custom dashboard on the actor’s primary server. LLM Key Theft 2,233 API keys harvested * Keys from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and DeepSeek * **12** marked valid by the actor’s own tooling * **247** exposed LLM gateways catalogued, serving models from these providers and Meta Academic Fraud 20 Institutions targeted, 19 in the US * **195** Harvard alumni records from a torrent-distributed dataset tied to the November 2025 ShinyHunters incident * Application payment links for Stanford, UChicago, Wake Forest, Case Western and Central Michigan * Accounts created at NYU, UC Berkeley, Oregon State, the University of Illinois, Colorado State and others Financial Fraud 3 Parallel fraud channels * Harmony ONE cryptocurrency drainer * Credit card validation with stolen Stripe merchant API keys * Second-hand CVVs sourced from a Chinese underground market Directory listing was enabled on the actor’s primary server. This exposed tools, scripts, logs and Telegram bot tokens, including tokens for the actor’s own AI agent bots. Tenspresso, a three month old chip startup, is in talks for a $500 million valuation Tenspresso's 15-person team, stacked with Google TPU veterans, hasn't finished designing a chip and won't until 2027 or 2028, yet Altimeter Capital is already pushing its valuation toward Etched-startup territory. ![](https://startupfortune.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/08/elroy.png) [Elroy Fernandes](https://startupfortune.com/author/elroy/) · 4 min read · 593 reads ![Tenspresso, a three month old chip startup, is in talks for a $500 million valuation](https://startupfortune.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/tenspresso-dong-hyuk-woo-altimeter-capital-1024x576.jpg) *Investors are chasing a 15 person AI chip startup that doesn't yet have a finished design, pricing scarce engineering talent over any actual product.* Tenspresso was not a company three months ago. Now, according to a report from Bloomberg, the Sunnyvale startup is in talks to raise at least $50 million in a round that would value it at $500 million. Altimeter Capital Management is the firm driving the new conversation, and it's doing so only weeks after Tenspresso closed a $20 million seed round led by Striker Venture Partners. The company was co-founded by Dong Hyuk Woo and Harshit Khaitan, two engineers who spent years together building Google's tensor processing units before striking out on their own. That pedigree is doing most of the work here. Tenspresso's 15 person team is stacked with alumni from Google's early TPU effort, and in a market where that kind of experience is scarce, Altimeter and Striker appear willing to pay for the roster before there's a product to show for it. There is no chip yet. Tenspresso aims to finish designing its first product in late 2027 or early 2028, Bloomberg reported, which means a $500 million valuation would rest entirely on an architecture and a team, not silicon, not customers, not a single benchmark. The company is building for inference, specifically chips meant to handle long context windows so AI models can chew through larger and more varied pools of data at once. That's a real and growing bottleneck for anyone running big models in production, but it's also a bet two years out from being testable. Infra & Chips.titleZh: Supermicro will sell SambaNova’s inference chips alongside Nvidia GPUs
Infra & Chips.content: Supermicro will build and sell AI inference systems that pair SambaNova’s SN50 chips with Nvidia GPUs, the companies said on Tuesday. The collaboration initially plans for 10,000 SN50 chips, according to SambaNova’s announcement. The racks will join Supermicro’s Data Center Building Block Solutions, the ready-made data centre systems it sells to customers. Running an AI model has two stages. First the system reads the prompt, then it writes the answer piece by piece. In the new racks, Nvidia GPUs do the reading and SN50 chips do the writing, SambaNova said. The company says AI agents work nonstop, so how fast they act depends on how fast the model responds. > “Agentic AI is the next wave of inference, and it has to run everywhere,” said Rodrigo Liang, co-founder and chief executive of SambaNova. “Now customers can order SN50 RDUs alongside GPUs, from a world-leading partner they trust.” ## Who does what Supermicro will put the systems together, test them, deliver them and support customers, including with on-site service. SambaNova engineers will get AI models running and tuned on SN50 and help with deployments. The companies will start with neoclouds, the cloud providers built for AI, and with sovereign clouds. Those keep data and computing inside one country. They then plan to sell to companies that run AI in their own data centres. > “Supermicro is committed to delivering flexible, high-performance AI infrastructure that supports the evolving requirements of our customers,” said Charles Liang, president and chief executive of Supermicro. ## Built for existing data centres SN50 is SambaNova’s fifth-generation Reconfigurable Dataflow Unit, or RDU, a chip designed for inference. The company says it can serve the largest models without needing extreme power density in each rack. A SambaRack SN50 draws an average of 20 kW, SambaNova said last week. Operators can add inference capacity in data centres they already run, according to SambaNova. They do not have to wait for new builds held back by power and cooling. It says they can also keep using their existing GPUs for longer. The two companies say they can deliver much more inference capacity in 2027 as a result. ## SambaNova’s other recent deals The Supermicro deal follows another one with Oracle. Oracle said at its AI World conference on 27 October that it plans to deploy SN50 chips in its cloud data centres. It will offer the capacity to AI model builders. Two days later, SambaNova signed Emergys, a digital transformation services company, to deploy and run its platform for enterprise customers. SambaNova, founded in 2017 and based in San Jose, raised new funding at an $11 billion valuation in July. (Photo: THE ELEC)](https://cdn.thelec.net/news/photo/202611/15270_15576_5355.jpg) Keith Strier, AMD's senior vice president of global AI markets. (Photo: THE ELEC) AMD will partner with FuriosaAI and MangoBoost to build a heterogeneous artificial intelligence (AI) computing infrastructure cluster in Seoul next year. Keith Strier, AMD's senior vice president of global AI markets, announced the plan at the AMD Advancing AI Seoul 2026 event held at the Westin Seoul Parnas in Samseong-dong on Nov. 4. "We will sign a memorandum of understanding (MOU) with FuriosaAI and MangoBoost shortly," he said. "We plan to establish the first reference cluster in Seoul next spring, using heterogeneous AI computing infrastructure that integrates processors from all three companies." Heterogeneous computing combines different types of semiconductors to improve computational efficiency. The platform being developed by the three companies will integrate AMD's central processing units (CPUs) and graphics processing units (GPUs) with FuriosaAI's neural processing units (NPUs) and MangoBoost's data processing units (DPUs). FuriosaAI develops and supplies its proprietary Renegade (RNGD) NPU, a chip designed specifically for AI inference in data centers. The company began mass production of its second-generation RNGD in January this year. FuriosaAI claims the chip delivers 1.7 to 1.8 times the performance of Nvidia's H100 at the same power consumption. It has signed a technology validation agreement with LG AI Research and supplied chips to Upstage. MangoBoost's DPU is called BoostX. The chip handles communications, storage input/output and security processing in AI infrastructure. These tasks have traditionally consumed CPU computing resources. By offloading them to a DPU, CPUs can focus on their primary computing workloads. BoostX accelerates GPU communications and storage using standard Ethernet technology. Integrating AMD hardware with Korean-made semiconductors was among the initiatives included in an MOU signed by AMD and South Korea's Ministry of Science and ICT at the AI Summit in San Francisco in July this year. The two sides agreed to jointly develop and demonstrate heterogeneous AI computing infrastructure combining AMD chips with Korean AI NPUs. AMD CEO Lisa Su further detailed the initiative during her visit to South Korea in October. She pledged to develop the infrastructure into a reference model for use in global markets. AMD also announced plans to establish an AI Center of Excellence (CoE) with the Ministry of Science and ICT. Election results in Texas and Ohio point to stricter review of AI infrastructure projects. ![](https://f1.tokenpost.com/2024/11/9vga9k0r6d.png) By **[Enna Lee](/reporters/24)** Published ![Sealed hardware crates sit inside an unfinished data-center structure / TokenPost.ai](https://mzwrodgsdjfdyvnraeya.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/article-media/articles/a87e2bc03c5773435da4ede19ec0b6af040861714ea06daef5eda6dc48f2f044.webp) Sealed hardware crates sit inside an unfinished data-center structure / TokenPost.ai Nvidia shares rose Wednesday, Nov. 4, as recent upbeat results from leading chip companies suggested that concerns about data-center construction delays had not yet affected Nvidia and other hardware firms, even as U.S. election results pointed to stricter project review. Customers continued stockpiling AI hardware despite uncertainty over where suitable installation sites would be available. Recent positive results from leading chip companies suggested construction delays had not immediately affected Nvidia or other hardware makers. Republican governors in Texas and Ohio lost their elections, meaning AI infrastructure projects will face stricter review. Nvidia would face a greater challenge if Democratic officials pursue strict limits on data-center construction. Infra & Chips.content: # SambaNova partners with Supermicro for SN50 RDU deployments Server maker will initially purchase 10,000 SN50 chips from SambaNova SambaNova has partnered with Supermicro for the deployment of SN50 RDU chips. In a statement, SambaNova said Supermicro would initially purchase 10,000 SN50 RDUs from the AI chip company in order to build and sell AI disaggregated inference systems. Those Supermicro systems will comprise both Nvidia GPUs and SambaNova RDUs, with the server maker set to integrate, test, deliver, and support the systems for customers, including providing on-site service. Meanwhile, engineers from SambaNova will ensure AI models are tuned to run on the SN50 chips, and will support Supermicro with deployments, starting with neoclouds and sovereign cloud providers, before expanding to enterprises looking to run AI in their own data centers. SambaNova first unveiled the chips, dubbed SN50 AI, in February 2026, stating that the hardware had been designed to support agentic AI workloads. At the time, the company claimed the RDUs were 5x faster than “competitive chips,” offering a 3x lower total cost of ownership, although it did not name the comparative hardware. Built using the company’s Reconfigurable Data Unit (RDU) architecture, SN50 features a three-tier memory design that supports ten-trillion-parameter models and can power “thousands of simultaneous AI sessions with consistent high performance.” SambaNova added that the chip also offers 4x more network bandwidth than its previous generation, and up to 256 accelerators can be linked over a multi-terabyte-per-second interconnect. "Agentic AI is the next wave of inference, and it has to run everywhere," said Rodrigo Liang, co-founder and CEO of SambaNova. "Supermicro builds AI infrastructure for data centers globally. Now customers can order SN50 RDUs alongside GPUs, from a world-leading partner they trust. That's how fast, efficient inference gets to scale." Charles Liang, president and CEO of Supermicro, added: “Supermicro is committed to delivering flexible, high-performance AI infrastructure that supports the evolving requirements of our customers. Our collaboration with SambaNova expands our broad DCBBS portfolio by enabling heterogeneous architectures that integrate GPU computing with specialized inference acceleration, helping customers deploy efficient, scalable AI solutions.” Founded in 2017, SambaNova previously focused on training workloads, but pivoted in 2025 to become an AI cloud services provider. Its Suite product is touted as an on-prem or cloud-based offering that allows companies to train their own generative AI models based on popular foundation models. The company first unveiled its SambaNova Cloud in September 2024. It provides cloud-based AI inference services using the company’s SN40L AI chip, launched in September 2023 and capable of running models with up to five trillion parameters.

Infra & Chips.content: ## Since 1987: Covering the Fastest Computers in the World and the People Who Run Them ### TCI Media: Home of the Wire Publications ![Header Logo 1](https://www.hpcwire.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/ai-600-300x73-1.webp) ![Header Logo 2](https://www.hpcwire.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/data-600-300x72-1.webp) ![Header Logo 3](https://www.hpcwire.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/qc-600-300x69-1.webp) ![Logo](https://www.hpcwire.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/hpc-logo-300x60-1.jpg) ## Off the Wire Press Releases ### November 4, 2026 ### November 3, 2026 ## SambaNova and Supermicro to Build AI Inference Systems Combining RDUs and GPUs SAN JOSE, Calif., Nov. 4, 2026 — [SambaNova](https://sambanova.ai/) has announced that [Supermicro](https://www.supermicro.com/) is entering into a strategic collaboration, initially planning for 10,000 SN50 RDU chips, to build and sell AI disaggregated inference systems that include RDUs and GPUs. [![](https://www.hpcwire.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/SambaNova_x_Supermicro_Logos-300x169.jpg)](https://www.hpcwire.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/SambaNova_x_Supermicro_Logos.jpg)“Agentic AI is the next wave of inference, and it has to run everywhere,” said Rodrigo Liang, co-founder and CEO of SambaNova. “Supermicro builds AI infrastructure for data centers globally. Now customers can order SN50 RDUs alongside GPUs, from a world-leading partner they trust. That’s how fast, efficient inference gets to scale.” ![](https://www.hpcwire.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/SambaNova_x_Supermicro_Logos-300x169.jpg) Agents work nonstop, and how fast they act depends on how fast the model responds. Supermicro’s systems pair NVIDIA GPUs, which read the prompt, with SambaNova SN50 chips built to write the response quickly. “Supermicro is committed to delivering flexible, high-performance AI infrastructure that supports the evolving requirements of our customers. Our collaboration with SambaNova expands our broad DCBBS portfolio by enabling heterogeneous architectures that integrate GPU computing with specialized inference acceleration, helping customers deploy efficient, scalable AI solutions,” said Charles Liang, president and CEO of Supermicro. **Built, Sold and Supported by Supermicro** Supermicro will integrate, test, deliver and support the systems for customers, including providing on-site service. SambaNova engineers will get models running and tuned on SN50 and help Supermicro with deployments. The companies will start with NeoClouds and sovereign clouds, then expand to enterprises that run AI in their own data centers. **About SambaNova RDU Chips** SambaNova’s SN50 is the company’s fifth-generation Reconfigurable Dataflow Unit (RDU) chip, purpose-built for high-performance inference. RDUs serve the largest models at high speed and high throughput without requiring extreme rack power density, which makes them much easier to deploy in existing data centers. RDUs also work alongside existing NVIDIA GPUs to drastically improve system performance and efficiency, with the GPUs running the prefill phase and the RDUs running the decode phase. Operators can therefore add inference capacity without waiting for next-generation data center build-outs, which are constrained by power and cooling, and can extend the useful life of the GPUs they already own. As a result, SambaNova and Supermicro can deliver substantially more high-performance inference capacity in 2027 than would otherwise be possible. **About SambaNova** [SambaNova](https://sambanova.ai/) is a leader in next-generation AI infrastructure, providing a full stack platform that powers high-performance inference for enterprises, NeoClouds, AI labs and service providers, and sovereign AI initiatives worldwide. Founded in 2017 and headquartered in San Jose, Calif., SambaNova delivers chips, systems, and cloud services that enable customers to deploy state-of-the-art models with superior performance, lower total cost of ownership, and rapid time to value. *Source...
